title: From Locking to Collective Chaos: A Reproducible Review of Kaneko's Circle Maps, Torus Instabilities, Coupled Map Lattices and Globally Coupled Maps
affil: Laboratory of Fluid Mechanics and Instabilities, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, CH-1015 Lausanne, Switzerland
lede: A reference atlas of Kunihiko Kaneko's 1982–1998 models—circle maps, torus instabilities, coupled map lattices and globally coupled maps—in which every figure regenerates from one open-source dynachaos command.
abstract: Kunihiko Kaneko’s papers of 1982–1998 traced how ordered dynamics lose order: phase locking, torus oscillation, doubling and fractalization, symmetry breaking, three-frequency motion, spatiotemporal intermittency, and collective chaos in globally coupled maps. This review recomputes figures from those papers with the open-source package dynachaos and arranges the models in six steps, from phase locking to mean-field coupling. Each figure names the command that regenerates it. Parameter scans use up to 2×105 values. Four modern diagnostics—the 0-1 test, SALI, permutation entropy, and recurrence quantification analysis—are examined alongside classical measures; in the runs shown here on a dissipative map, SALI decays in every regime and does not separate regular from chaotic motion. The review adds no new route to chaos and no new diagnostic; the torus-doubling exponent is quoted from Kaneko, not remeasured, and whether the spatiotemporal intermittency of the lattices shown here belongs to the directed-percolation class, as measured in circle-map lattices and in experiment, is not tested. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
